concept.name: Model evaluation
concept.definition: The systematic measurement of a model's or AI system's performance, behavior, and risks against defined criteria, datasets, and contexts of use. In the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, evaluation sits in the MEASURE function: risks and trustworthiness characteristics are identified, measured, and tracked with appropriate metrics and testing throughout the lifecycle.
concept.intuition: Report cards with a rubric: you decide in advance what 'good' means, test against data the model did not train on, and record the results so regressions are visible.
concept.mechanics: Evaluation combines quantitative metrics (accuracy, calibration, task benchmarks) computed on held-out or golden datasets, behavioral testing (adversarial probes, edge cases), and human review; results feed go/no-go decisions, monitoring baselines, and drift detection. Effective evaluation matches metrics and test sets to the actual deployment context rather than generic benchmarks.
concept.failure_modes: Evaluation on data that leaks into training inflates measured performance; static benchmarks saturate and stop discriminating; metrics chosen for convenience (accuracy on imbalanced data) mislead about deployment behavior. One-time pre-deployment evaluation misses post-deployment drift.
concept.misconceptions: A high benchmark score is not evidence of fitness for a specific task — benchmarks measure benchmark performance. Evaluation is also not a one-time gate; NIST frames measurement as continuous across the AI lifecycle.
concept.example: Before a knowledge assistant answers compliance questions, it is evaluated on a held-out golden dataset of 200 expert-annotated Q&A pairs, with accuracy, citation correctness, and abstention rate all reported per domain.
